title: First Parliamentary Election in Bangladesh
subtitle: Bangladesh held its first national parliamentary election on 7 March 1973.
summary: Bangladesh held its first parliamentary election as an independent state on 7 March 1973, under the parliamentary order established by the 1972 Constitution. The Bangladesh Awami League contested all 300 directly elected seats and won 293, taking 73.2 percent of votes cast; the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal won one seat. The result gave Prime Minister Sheikh Mujibur Rahman’s party a commanding legislative majority in the new republic.
heroTagline: The Awami League won 293 of 300 directly elected seats on 7 March 1973.
whyItMatters: The poll converted the post-independence constitutional framework into an elected national legislature. Its overwhelming seat distribution gave the Awami League a dominant position in parliament, making the first election both a landmark in institutional formation and an important baseline for studying Bangladesh’s early party competition.

claimCitations.claim: Bangladesh held its first parliamentary election as an independent state on 7 March 1973, under the parliamentary order established by the 1972 Constitution. The Bangladesh Awami League contested all 300 directly elected seats and won 293, taking 73.2 percent of votes cast; the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal won one seat. The result gave Prime Minister Sheikh Mujibur Rahman’s party a commanding legislative majority in the new republic.

The poll converted the post-independence constitutional framework into an elected national legislature. Its overwhelming seat distribution gave the Awami League a dominant position in parliament, making the first election both a landmark in institutional formation and an important baseline for studying Bangladesh’s early party competition.
The 1973 election established the first elected Jatiya Sangsad of independent Bangladesh and set the initial pattern of parliamentary representation under the 1972 Constitution.
As the first parliamentary vote after independence, it became a reference point for accounts of Bangladesh’s transition from liberation to constitutional government.
